drhp.business: Viaz Tyres manufactures rubber tubes for bicycles, two and three wheelers, passenger vehicles and heavy load industrial vehicles, and also deals in ancillary products such as OTR tyre tubes, ADV tubes, and white-labelled engine oil and grease. It has recently started selling job-work bicycle tyres, trades tyres in Turkey through an exclusive distributorship with Maxxis Rubbers Private Limited, and sells across domestic and international markets under its own brand names.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic India (19 states)|United States of America|Turkey|Romania|United Arab Emirates|Colombia
drhp.expansion: Viaz is building a new tyre manufacturing facility, in addition to its existing tube plant, to manufacture up to 16 lakh tyres annually across two-wheeler, three-wheeler, light commercial vehicle and agricultural applications, funded through phased capital expenditure with a total planned outlay of Rs 50-55 crore. During FY26 the Company continued to invest in this facility as part of its transition from being an inner-tube manufacturer to a complete tyre and rubber-products company.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Tyre demand is supported by two engines: OEM (new-vehicle) demand and replacement demand from the installed vehicle population, with replacement estimated at approximately 54% of industry tyre volumes (ATMA/PwC, FY24), giving a broad and recurring demand base.
- FY26 was a strong year for Indian auto sales across all four principal vehicle categories (each at 7-year highs), supporting healthy OEM demand for tyres.
- Two- and three-wheeler tyres form the largest category of Indian tyre production by volume (~53%), aligning with Viaz's chosen focus segments.
- A growing and ageing installed vehicle …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Viaz is building a new tyre manufacturing facility, in addition to its existing tube plant, to manufacture up to 16 lakh tyres annually across two-wheeler, three-wheeler, light commercial vehicle and agricultural applications, funded through phased capital expenditure with a total planned outlay of Rs 50-55 crore. During FY26 the Company continued to invest in this facility as part of its transition from being an inner-tube manufacturer to a complete tyre and rubber-products company.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: Established multi-state and international dealer/distributor network — evidence: distribution network spread across 19 states and presence in 5 countries with 7 international distributors
- integration: Existing rubber-processing, compounding, mixing, moulding and quality-control capability from the tube business is being carried into tyre manufacturing — evidence: nearly two decades of operating knowledge in rubber and tube manufacturing cited in the MD&A

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Rubber, carbon black, chemicals and crude-linked inputs are susceptible to price fluctuations; sudden increases can compress margins where selling-price revisions occur with a lag.
- Installed capacity at the new tyre facility does not automatically translate into revenue; utilisation depends on product qualification, channel penetration, manufacturing yield and market acceptance.
- The Indian tyre industry includes several established domestic and multinational manufacturers with significant brand equity, distribution and R&D capability; Viaz is entering from a relatively small base.
- The manufacturing transformation into tyres requires knowledge-intensive activities (formulation, mixing, extrusion, curing, process control, testing), making technical training, process discipline and retention of skilled personnel important as operations scale.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build capacity utilisation across both the existing tube business and the new tyre facility as the first growth lever.
- Shift product mix towards complete tyres, which carry higher realisation than inner tubes, to raise blended revenue per unit.
- Deepen and progressively expand a Pan-India dealer/distribution network, focused on markets with attractive replacement demand.
- Pursue backward integration and cost efficiency through reclaimed rubber/tyre recycling capability and renewable/solar power for manufacturing.
- Move towards specialisation in higher-value applications across agricultural, …
